question: Should a touring band use backing tracks to reproduce its layered studio sound on stage?
sides: No, play only what is played
answer: A modern record is dozens of layers: stacked vocals, doubled guitars, synth pads. Four people cannot play forty parts, and an audience paid to hear the songs it knows. Tracks let a small band deliver the arrangement faithfully every night, while the players and the singer stay genuinely live on top of them.
move: Whichever side you took, it turns on whether a ticket buys songs or performance.
counterpoint: A concert is worth attending because it can differ from the record. Tracks lock every song to a click, so the band cannot stretch a chorus or follow the crowd. When they fail, the illusion collapses, as when the wrong vocal track played for Ashlee Simpson on Saturday Night Live in 2004.
reference: Saturday Night Live, NBC, broadcast 23 October 2004
